text: The Cape Town Cycle Tour, formerly known as the Cape Argus Cycle Tour, is an annual cycle race held in Cape Town, South Africa, typically covering a distance of 109 km (68 mi). It is the first event outside Europe to be included in the Union Cycliste Internationale's Golden Bike Series. South Africa hosts three of the world's largest sporting events by number of entrants, with the Cape Town Cycle Tour, which can attract up to 35,000 cyclists, being the world's largest individually timed cycle race. The other two are the Comrades Marathon, the world's largest ultra-marathon running event, and the Midmar Mile, the world's largest open water swim. The Cycle Tour was the final leg of the Giro del Capo, a multi-stage race for professional and leading registered riders, which was last held in 2010. Traditionally staged on the second Sunday of March, the event has featured well-known competitors such as Miguel Indurain, Jan Ulrich, Matt Damon, Helen Zille, and Lance Armstrong. The race usually follows a scenic 109 km circular route starting at Grand Parade in Cape Town, traveling along Nelson Mandela Boulevard (N2), the M3 to Muizenberg, Main Road along the False Bay coast to Simon's Town and Smitswinkel Bay, then crossing the peninsula westward past the entrance to the Cape of Good Hope section of Table Mountain National Park (including Cape Point), heading north along the Atlantic coast through Scarborough, Kommetjie, Noordhoek, Chapman's Peak, Hout Bay over Suikerbossie Hill to Camps Bay, and ending near the Cape Town Stadium in Green Point. Between 2009 and 2010, and prior to 1999, the route varied in length between 104 km (65 mi) and 110 km (68 mi). The course records for conventional bicycles on the 110 km course over Chapman's Peak are documented. Penny Krohn holds the record for the most consecutive age group victories with 25. The fastest time ever recorded—also the highest average speed—was set in 1993 on the 105 km course by Wimpie van der Merwe in a fully faired recumbent, completing it in 02:16:40 at an average speed of 46.1 km/h. Japie Malan, at 92 years old during the 2012 Cycle Tour, is the oldest cyclist to complete the race within the seven-hour limit on a tandem, finishing in 05:49:00; he is also the oldest man (90 years old at the time) to complete the race on a single bicycle during the 2010 Cycle Tour, finishing in 06:48:52, and the oldest man to ride the Argus for the first time, which he did in 2004 at age 84. Mary Warner, at 80 years old during the 2006 tour, is the oldest woman to complete the race, finishing in 06:43:38. In 1978, Bill Mylrea and John Stegmann organized the Big Ride-In to advocate for cycle paths in South Africa, which drew hundreds of cyclists, including the Mayor of Cape Town at the time, and was first won by Lawrence Whittaker in September 1978. The original plan for the race was 140 km (87 mi), including a leg to Cape Point, but it was reduced to 104 km (65 mi) after being denied entry to the then Cape Point Nature Reserve; organizers convinced the initially reluctant Cape Argus, a local newspaper and sponsor, to allow the event to use its name. The event is now part of a week-long series of five cycling events that begin a week before the Cycle Tour and conclude with the main race. Between 2000 and 2003, the route was altered due to the closure of Chapman's Peak Drive, with a return via Ou Kaapse Weg and the Blue Route. The race has been halted three times due to extreme weather—twice when many competitors had already completed it, and once significantly shortened due to fire—and once cancelled.
